courses.title: Islamic Studies — Primary (Grade 1-5)
courses.subject: Basic Islamic Studies
courses.description: A gentle introduction to the foundations of Islam for young learners — pillars of faith, Prophet stories, daily duas, and good manners.
courses.longDescription:
This course introduces primary school students (Grades 1-5) to the core building blocks of Islamic belief and practice in a simple, age-appropriate way. Students learn the Five Pillars of Islam and the Six Pillars of Iman, hear the stories of beloved Prophets, and memorize short daily duas for everyday moments like waking up, eating, and leaving home.

The course also walks students step by step through wudu and Salah so they can begin praying with confidence, and closes with lessons on Islamic manners (Akhlaq) — honesty, kindness to parents, and good behavior with neighbors and friends. Lessons combine short videos, hands-on drawing/craft assignments, and simple quizzes to reinforce memorization and understanding.
objectives: Recite and explain the Five Pillars of Islam and Six Pillars of Iman
Retell simple stories of the Prophets and identify the lessons within them
Memorize and correctly use short daily duas
Perform wudu and pray a basic Salah with correct movements
Demonstrate good Islamic manners at home and with others

assignments.title: Draw and Label the Five Pillars
assignments.description: Draw a large poster showing all five pillars of Islam as separate pictures (e.g. a mosque for Salah, a moneybox for Zakat). Label each picture with its correct name. Write one sentence under each picture explaining what it means. Color your poster neatly and bring it to class to present in two minutes.

assignments.title: My Iman Booklet
assignments.description: Create a small 6-page booklet, one page for each pillar of Iman. On each page, write the name of the belief and draw a picture that represents it. Under the picture, write one sentence in your own words explaining what you believe. Staple the pages together to make your booklet.

assignments.title: Retell a Prophet's Story
assignments.description: Choose one Prophet's story from this module (Adam, Ibrahim, or Yunus). Write a short retelling of the story in 6-8 sentences using your own words. Draw one picture showing the most important part of the story. Be ready to share your story out loud with the class.

assignments.title: Dua Memorization Chart
assignments.description: Make a chart with four boxes, one for each dua learned in this module. Write out each dua in Arabic (or transliteration) and its English meaning in the correct box. Practice reciting each dua at the correct time for one full week. Ask a parent to sign the chart confirming you practiced.

assignments.title: Wudu and Salah Practice Log
assignments.description: For five days, practice performing wudu correctly before each prayer. Keep a simple daily log noting which prayer you performed and whether you remembered every step of wudu. Ask a parent or older sibling to watch you once and give feedback. Submit your completed log at the end of the week.

assignments.title: Good Manners Diary
assignments.description: Keep a diary for three days where you write down one kind or honest action you did each day (e.g. helping a parent, telling the truth in a hard situation). Write 2-3 sentences describing what you did and how it made you feel. Also write one thing you want to improve about your manners.

courses.title: Islamic Studies — Middle School (Grade 6-8)
courses.subject: Basic Islamic Studies
courses.description: A deeper study of the Prophet's life, Hadith, Fiqh, Islamic history, Quranic themes, character, and world religions for middle schoolers.
courses.longDescription:
Building on primary-level foundations, this course takes Grade 6-8 students through the Seerah of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in more historical detail, introduces the science of Hadith and its major collections, and covers the Fiqh of worship (Salah, Sawm, Zakat, Hajj) with practical rulings. Students also study the early Islamic Caliphate and the spread of Islam.

The course then turns to major themes in the Quran, the development of strong Islamic character (Sabr, Shukr, honesty, avoiding backbiting), and closes with a respectful, age-appropriate introduction to other major world religions — helping students understand their own faith more deeply while engaging thoughtfully with a diverse world.
objectives: Explain key events in the Seerah of Prophet Muhammad (SAW) with approximate dates and significance
Define Hadith terminology and identify the major hadith collections
Apply basic fiqh rulings related to Salah, Sawm, Zakat and Hajj
Describe the achievements of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs
Identify major Quranic themes and extract lessons from Quranic stories
Demonstrate understanding of core Islamic character traits
Compare basic beliefs of Islam with other major world religions respectfully

assignments.title: Seerah Timeline Project
assignments.description: Create a timeline poster of the Prophet Muhammad's (SAW) life from birth to the Hijrah, including at least 8 key events with dates and one-sentence descriptions. Use images or simple drawings to illustrate at least three events. Write a short paragraph (5-6 sentences) explaining which event you find most inspiring and why. Submit your timeline as a poster or a typed document.

assignments.title: Hadith Reflection Essay
assignments.description: Choose one hadith studied in this module and write a 200-300 word reflection. Explain the meaning of the hadith, the context in which it was said if known, and how you can apply its lesson in your own life this week. Include the Arabic text or translation of the hadith at the top of your essay. Proofread your essay before submitting.

assignments.title: Compare the Five Prayers Chart
assignments.description: Create a table comparing the five daily prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. For each prayer, list the number of rakahs (Sunnah and Fard), the approximate time window, and one fiqh ruling specific to that prayer. Research using a reliable Islamic source if needed. Submit your completed chart.

assignments.title: Profile of a Rightly Guided Caliph
assignments.description: Select one of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, or Ali) and write a one-page biography. Cover his relationship to the Prophet (SAW), key achievements during his caliphate, and one major challenge he faced. Use at least two specific historical events as evidence. Cite where you found your information.

assignments.title: Quranic Theme Presentation
assignments.description: Prepare a short 5-slide presentation on one major Quran theme covered in this module (Tawheed, Prophethood, Justice, or a Quranic story). Include at least two verses (with translation) that support the theme. Explain in your own words what the theme teaches Muslims today. Be ready to present for 3-4 minutes in class.

assignments.title: Character Self-Assessment Journal
assignments.description: Over one week, keep a daily journal entry (3-4 sentences per day) reflecting on a moment where you practiced or struggled with one of the virtues studied in this module (patience, gratitude, honesty, or avoiding backbiting). At the end of the week, write a short summary paragraph identifying one area you want to improve and how.

assignments.title: Comparative Religion Summary Table
assignments.description: Create a table comparing Islam, Christianity, Judaism, Hinduism and Buddhism across four categories: view of God, holy book(s), view of the afterlife, and main place of worship. Write a short closing paragraph (4-5 sentences) on what you learned about respecting people of other faiths while holding firmly to your own beliefs. Use only respectful, accurate language throughout.
